claim: The integrated stress response (ISR) comprises four stress-regulated kinases – PERK, PKR, GCN2, and HRI – that selectively phosphorylate eIF2α in response to diverse pathologic insults.
source: The integrated stress response (ISR) comprises four stress-regulated kinases – PERK, PKR, GCN2, and HRI – that selectively phosphorylate eIF2α in response to diverse pathologic insults (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020 and Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016

claim: The ISR has recently emerged as a prominent stress-responsive signaling pathway activated by different types of mitochondrial stress.
source: The ISR has recently emerged as a prominent stress-responsive signaling pathway activated by different types of mitochondrial stress (Anderson and Haynes, 2020; Quirós et al., 2016; Winter et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Anderson and Haynes, 2020; Quirós et al., 2016; Winter et al., 2022

claim: Mitochondrial uncoupling or inhibition of ATP synthase activates the ISR through a mechanism involving the cytosolic accumulation and oligomerization of the mitochondrial protein DELE1, which binds to and activates the ISR kinase HRI.
source: Mitochondrial uncoupling or inhibition of ATP synthase activates the ISR through a mechanism involving the cytosolic accumulation and oligomerization of the mitochondrial protein DELE1, which binds to and activates the ISR kinase HRI (Fessler et al., 2020; Fessler et al., 2022; Guo et al., 2020; Sekine et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2023a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fessler et al., 2020; Fessler et al., 2022; Guo et al., 2020; Sekine et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2023a

claim: Complex I inhibition can activate the ISR downstream of the ISR kinase GCN2.
source: Complex I inhibition can also activate the ISR downstream of the ISR kinase GCN2 (Mick et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mick et al., 2020

claim: CRISPRi-depletion of mitochondrial proteostasis factors preferentially activates the ISR over other stress-responsive signaling pathways.
source: Further, CRISPRi-depletion of mitochondrial proteostasis factors preferentially activates the ISR over other stress-responsive signaling pathways (Madrazo et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citation to Madrazo et al., 2024

claim: ISR kinases are activated in response to stress through a conserved mechanism involving dimerization and autophosphorylation.
source: ISR kinases are activated in response to stress through a conserved mechanism involving dimerization and autophosphorylation (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016

claim: Once activated, ISR kinases phosphorylate eIF2α, resulting in both a transient attenuation of new protein synthesis and the activation of stress-responsive transcription factors such as ATF4.
source: Once activated, these kinases phosphorylate eIF2α, resulting in both a transient attenuation of new protein synthesis and the activation of stress-responsive transcription factors such as ATF4 (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016

claim: The activation of ATF4 downstream of phosphorylated eIF2α transcriptionally regulates the expression of mitochondrial chaperones (e.g., the mitochondrial HSP70 HSPA9) and proteases (e.g., the AAA+ protease LONP1), increasing mitochondrial proteostasis capacity during stress.
source: For example, the activation of ATF4 downstream of phosphorylated eIF2α transcriptionally regulates the expression of mitochondrial chaperones (e.g., the mitochondrial HSP70 HSPA9) and proteases (e.g., the AAA+ protease LONP1), increasing mitochondrial proteostasis capacity during stress (Hori et al., 2002; Han et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hori et al., 2002; Han et al., 2013

claim: ISR-dependent translational attenuation enhances mitochondrial proteostasis through the selective degradation of the core import subunit TIM17A, which slows mitochondrial protein import and reduces the load of newly synthesized proteins entering mitochondria during stress.
source: ISR-dependent translational attenuation also enhances mitochondrial proteostasis through the selective degradation of the core import subunit TIM17A, which slows mitochondrial protein import and reduces the load of newly synthesized proteins entering mitochondria during stress (Rainbolt et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rainbolt et al., 2013

claim: Transcriptional and translational signaling induced by the activation of ISR kinases regulates many other mitochondrial functions, including phospholipid synthesis, cristae organization, and electron transport chain activity.
source: Apart from proteostasis, transcriptional and translational signaling induced by the activation of ISR kinases also regulates many other mitochondrial functions, including phospholipid synthesis, cristae organization, and electron transport chain activity (Balsa et al., 2019; Barad et al., 2023; Latorre-Muro et al., 2021; Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Balsa et al., 2019; Barad et al., 2023; Latorre-Muro et al., 2021; Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b

claim: Mitochondrial morphology is dictated by the relative activities of pro-fission and pro-fusion GTPases localized to the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes.
source: Mitochondrial morphology is dictated by the relative activities of pro-fission and pro-fusion GTPases localized to the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes (OMM and IMM, respectively) (Chan, 2020; Quintana-Cabrera and Scorrano, 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan, 2020; Quintana-Cabrera and Scorrano, 2023

claim: The pro-fusion GTPases MFN1 and MFN2 and the pro-fission GTPase DRP1 are all localized to the OMM.
source: These include the pro-fusion GTPases MFN1 and MFN2 and the pro-fission GTPase DRP1, all localized to the OMM.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about mitochondrial GTPases

claim: ER stress promotes adaptive mitochondrial elongation downstream of the PERK arm of the ISR through a mechanism involving the accumulation of the phospholipid phosphatidic acid on the OMM where it inhibits the pro-fission GTPase DRP1.
source: Previous results showed that ER stress promotes adaptive mitochondrial elongation downstream of the PERK arm of the ISR through a mechanism involving the accumulation of the phospholipid phosphatidic acid on the OMM where it inhibits the pro-fission GTPase DRP1 (Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b; Perea et al., 2023a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b; Perea et al., 2023a

claim: PERK-dependent increase of mitochondrial elongation functions to protect mitochondria during ER stress through multiple mechanisms, including enhanced regulation of respiratory chain activity, suppression of mitochondrial fragmentation, and reductions in the turnover of mitochondria by mitophagy.
source: This PERK-dependent increase of mitochondrial elongation functions to protect mitochondria during ER stress through multiple mechanisms, including enhanced regulation of respiratory chain activity, suppression of mitochondrial fragmentation, and reductions in the turnover of mitochondria by mitophagy (Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b; Perea et al., 2023a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b; Perea et al., 2023a

claim: Pharmacologic activation of the alternative ISR kinase GCN2 promotes adaptive mitochondrial elongation.
source: Apart from PERK, pharmacologic activation of the alternative ISR kinase GCN2 also promotes adaptive mitochondrial elongation (Perea et al., 2023a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Perea et al., 2023a

claim: Excessive mitochondrial fragmentation is a pathologic hallmark of numerous human diseases, including several neurodegenerative disorders.
source: Excessive mitochondrial fragmentation is a pathologic hallmark of numerous human diseases, including several neurodegenerative disorders (Chan, 2020; Sharma et al., 2021a; Chen et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2020; Sprenger and Langer, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan, 2020; Sharma et al., 2021a; Chen et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2020; Sprenger and Langer, 2019

claim: Fragmented mitochondria are often associated with mitochondrial dysfunctions, including impaired respiratory chain activity and dysregulation of mitophagy.
source: Fragmented mitochondria are often associated with mitochondrial dysfunctions, including impaired respiratory chain activity and dysregulation of mitophagy (Chan, 2020; Sharma et al., 2021a; Chen et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2020; Sprenger and Langer, 2019; Giacomello et al., 2020; Wai and Langer, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan, 2020; Sharma et al., 2021a; Chen et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2020; Sprenger and Langer, 2019; Giacomello et al., 2020; Wai and Langer, 2016

claim: Interventions that prevent mitochondrial fragmentation have been shown to correct pathologic mitochondrial dysfunction in models of many different diseases.
source: Consistent with this observation, interventions that prevent mitochondrial fragmentation have been shown to correct pathologic mitochondrial dysfunction in models of many different diseases (Whitley et al., 2019; Bhatti et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Whitley et al., 2019; Bhatti et al., 2023

claim: Genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of the pro-fission GTPase DRP1 blocks pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction in cellular and in vivo models of diverse neurodegenerative diseases, including Charcot–Marie–Tooth (CMT) Type 2A and Type 2B, spastic paraplegia, optic atrophy, Huntington's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Alzheimer's disease.
source: Notably, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of the pro-fission GTPase DRP1 blocks pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction in cellular and in vivo models of diverse neurodegenerative diseases, including Charcot–Marie–Tooth (CMT) Type 2A and Type 2B, spastic paraplegia, optic atrophy, Huntington's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Alzheimer's disease (Gu et al., 2022; Das et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2023b; Guo et al., 2013; Joshi et al., 2018; Bera et al., 2022; Manczak et al., 2016; Kandimalla et al., 2022; Yan et al., 2015; Baek et al., 2017; Mou and Li, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gu et al., 2022; Das et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2023b; Guo et al., 2013; Joshi et al., 2018; Bera et al., 2022; Manczak et al., 2016; Kandimalla et al., 2022; Yan et al., 2015; Baek et al., 2017; Mou and Li, 2019

claim: The small-molecule halofuginone is a potent activator of the ISR kinase GCN2 that promotes ISR-dependent, adaptive mitochondrial elongation.
source: Previous work identified the small-molecule halofuginone as a potent activator of the ISR kinase GCN2 that promotes ISR-dependent, adaptive mitochondrial elongation (Perea et al., 2023a; Keller et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Perea et al., 2023a; Keller et al., 2012

claim: The nucleoside mimetic compounds 0357 and 3610 preferentially activate the ISR downstream of the ISR kinase HRI.
source: Here, we used a small-molecule screening platform to identify two nucleoside mimetic compounds, 0357 and 3610, that preferentially activate the ISR downstream of the ISR kinase HRI.
evidence: Demonstrated through screening and validation experiments described in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic HRI activators 0357 and 3610 promote adaptive, ISR-dependent mitochondrial elongation.
source: Using these compounds, we demonstrate that pharmacologic HRI activators also promote adaptive, ISR-dependent mitochondrial elongation.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: Treatment with HRI-activating compounds or the GCN2 activator halofuginone prevents the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria induced by Ca2+ dysregulation.
source: Further, we show that treatment with these HRI-activating compounds or the GCN2 activator halofuginone prevents the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria induced by Ca2+ dysregulation
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: Compound-dependent activation of the ISR reduces the population of fragmented mitochondria and rescues basal mitochondrial network morphology in patient fibroblasts expressing the D414V variant of the pro-fusion GTPase MFN2.
source: Further, we show that compound-dependent activation of the ISR reduces the population of fragmented mitochondria and rescues basal mitochondrial network morphology in patient fibroblasts expressing the D414V variant of the pro-fusion GTPase MFN2 associated with a complex clinical phenotype including ataxia, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss (Sharma et al., 2021b).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript, with citation to Sharma et al., 2021b for the clinical phenotype

claim: The D414V variant of MFN2 is associated with a complex clinical phenotype including ataxia, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss.
source: patient fibroblasts expressing the D414V variant of the pro-fusion GTPase MFN2 associated with a complex clinical phenotype including ataxia, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss (Sharma et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sharma et al., 2021b

claim: Treatment with the calcium ionophore ionomycin induces rapid, DRP1-dependent mitochondrial fragmentation in cell culture models.
source: Treatment with the calcium ionophore ionomycin induces rapid, DRP1-dependent mitochondrial fragmentation in cell culture models (Ji et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ji et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2017

claim: The ATF4-FLuc translational reporter is activated by ISR-activating stressors including the ER stressor thapsigargin and the ATP synthase inhibitor oligomycin A.
source: We confirmed that ISR-activating stressors including the ER stressor thapsigargin (Tg) and the ATP synthase inhibitor oligomycin A (OA) robustly activated this reporter (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: The primary screen of the nucleoside mimetic analog compound library identified 34 hit compounds that activated the ATF4-FLuc reporter with a robust Z-score of greater than 3 fold.
source: Our primary screen identified 34 hit compounds that activated the ATF4-FLuc reporter with a robust Z-score of greater than 3 fold.
evidence: Reported as a result from the screening experiment

claim: After removing highly reactive compounds and pan-assay interference compounds (PAINS), the number of hits was reduced to 9.
source: We then removed highly reactive compounds and pan-assay interference compounds (PAINS), which reduced the number of hits to 9 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Reported as a result from the screening experiment, with structures shown in Figure 1B

claim: Compounds 0357 and 3610 most efficaciously activated the ATF4-FLuc reporter, albeit with low potency (EC50 > 10 µM).
source: This identified compounds 0357 and 3610 as the compounds that most efficaciously activated the ATF4-FLuc reporter, albeit with low potency (EC50 > 10 µM).
evidence: Reported as a result from dose-response experiments

claim: Co-treatment with the highly selective ISR inhibitor ISRIB blocked ATF4-FLuc activation induced by compounds 0357 and 3610.
source: We confirmed that co-treatment with the highly selective ISR inhibitor ISRIB (Sidrauski et al., 2013; Zyryanova et al., 2018) blocked ATF4-FLuc activation induced by these compounds, confirming this activation can be attributed to the ISR (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 1C and D, with citations to Sidrauski et al., 2013; Zyryanova et al., 2018 for ISRIB

claim: Treatment with 0357 or 3610 increased expression of the ISR target genes ASNS and CHAC1 in HEK293 and MEF cells.
source: Further, we used qPCR to show that treatment with 0357 or 3610 increased expression of the ISR target genes ASNS and CHAC1 in HEK293 and MEF cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E; Kreß et al., 2023; Grandjean et al., 2019).
evidence: Demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E, with citations to Kreß et al., 2023; Grandjean et al., 2019

claim: Compounds 0357 and 3610 did not activate luciferase reporters of other stress-responsive signaling pathways such as the unfolded protein response (UPR; XBP1-RLuc), the heat shock response (HSR; HSE-FLuc), or the oxidative stress response (OSR; ARE-FLuc).
source: Importantly, these compounds did not activate luciferase reporters of other stress-responsive signaling pathway such as the unfolded protein response (UPR; XBP1-RLuc) (Grandjean et al., 2020; Plate et al., 2016), the heat shock response (HSR; HSE-FLuc) (Calamini et al., 2011), or the oxidative stress response (OSR; ARE-FLuc) (Ibrahim et al., 2020; Figure 1E and F).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 1E and F, with citations to Grandjean et al., 2020; Plate et al., 2016; Calamini et al., 2011; Ibrahim et al., 2020

claim: Treatment with 0357 or 3610 did not induce expression of the UPR target gene BiP, the HSR target gene HSPA1A, or the OSR target gene NQO1 in HEK293 cells.
source: Further, treatment with these compounds did not induce expression of the UPR target gene BiP, the HSR target gene HSPA1A, or the OSR target gene NQO1 in HEK293 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Demonstrated through qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F

claim: Treatment with 0357 or 3610 did not significantly reduce viability of HEK293 cells.
source: Finally, treatment with 0357 or 3610 did not significantly reduce viability of HEK293 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Demonstrated through viability data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G

claim: CRISPRi-depletion of HRI, but no other ISR kinase, blocked ATF4-FLuc activation induced by compounds 0357 and 3610.
source: Treatment with either 0357 or 3610 activates the ATF4-mAPPLE reporter in control cells (Figure 1G and H). CRISPRi-depletion of HRI, but no other ISR kinase, blocked ATF4-FLuc activation induced by these two compounds.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 1G and H

claim: Treatment with conditions that induce mitochondrial elongation, such as the ER stressor thapsigargin and the GCN2 activator halofuginone, increased bounding box and ellipsoid principal axis length, while reducing sphericity.
source: Treatment with conditions that induce mitochondrial elongation, such as the ER stressor thapsigargin (Tg) and the GCN2 activator halofuginone (HF), increased bounding box and ellipsoid principal axis length, while reducing sphericity (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D) – all changes consistent with increases in mitochondrial length.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D

claim: Treatment with conditions that promote mitochondrial fragmentation, such as the mitochondrial uncouplers BtdCPU and CCCP, reduced bounding box length and ellipsoid principal axis length, while increasing sphericity.
source: In contrast, treatment with conditions that promote mitochondrial fragmentation, such as the mitochondrial uncouplers BtdCPU and CCCP (both compounds that activate HRI) (Fessler et al., 2020; Perea et al., 2023a), reduced bounding box length and ellipsoid principal axis length, while increasing sphericity (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D) – all changes consistent with increased mitochondrial fragmentation.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D, with citations to Fessler et al., 2020; Perea et al., 2023a

claim: Treatment with either 0357 or 3610 for 6 hr increased both the bounding box and ellipsoid principal axis length, while decreasing mitochondrial sphericity.
source: Treatment with either 0357 or 3610 for 6 hr increased both the bounding box and ellipsoid principal axis length, while decreasing mitochondrial sphericity (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 2A–D

claim: Co-treatment with the selective ISR inhibitor ISRIB blocked mitochondrial elongation induced by compounds 0357 and 3610.
source: Co-treatment with the selective ISR inhibitor ISRIB blocked these changes in mitochondria shape, indicating that these compounds induce mitochondrial elongation through an ISR-dependent mechanism (Figure 2E–H).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 2E–H

claim: ISRIB co-treatment blocked mitochondrial elongation induced by the ER stressor thapsigargin and the GCN2 activator halofuginone.
source: ISRIB co-treatment also blocked mitochondrial elongation induced by the ER stressor thapsigargin (Tg) and the GCN2 activator halofuginone (HF), as predicted (Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023a).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data, with citations to Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023a

claim: Ionomycin rapidly increased the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in MEFmtGFP cells, evidenced by reductions in both bounding box and ellipsoid principal axis length and increases of organelle sphericity.
source: As expected, ionomycin rapidly increased the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in these cells, evidenced by reductions in both bounding box and ellipsoid principal axis length and increases of organelle sphericity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D

claim: Pretreatment with the ER stressor thapsigargin reduced the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in ionomycin-treated cells.
source: Pretreatment with the ER stressor thapsigargin, which promotes stress-induced mitochondrial elongation downstream of the PERK ISR kinase, reduced the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in ionomycin-treated cells (Figure 3A–D), as previously reported (Perea et al., 2023b).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 3A–D, with citation to Perea et al., 2023b

claim: Treatment with halofuginone, 0357, or 3610 reduced the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in ionomycin-treated cells.
source: Intriguingly, treatment with halofuginone, 0357, or 3610 also reduced the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in ionomycin-treated cells. Instead, mitochondria in cells pretreated with these ISR kinase activators and challenged with ionomycin demonstrated mitochondrial lengths and sphericity similar to that observed in vehicle-treated MEFmtGFP cells (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 3A–D

claim: Over 150 pathogenic variants in the pro-fusion GTPase MFN2 are causatively associated with the autosomal-dominant peripheral neuropathy CMT Type 2A.
source: Over 150 pathogenic variants in the pro-fusion GTPase MFN2 are causatively associated with the autosomal-dominant peripheral neuropathy CMT Type 2A (Cartoni and Martinou, 2009; Zaman and Shutt, 2022; Alberti et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cartoni and Martinou, 2009; Zaman and Shutt, 2022; Alberti et al., 2024

claim: Many pathogenic MFN2 variants, including D414V, lead to increases in mitochondrial fragmentation.
source: While these pathogenic variants can impact diverse aspects of mitochondrial biology (Zaman and Shutt, 2022), many, including D414V, lead to increases in mitochondrial fragmentation (Sharma et al., 2021b; Cartoni and Martinou, 2009; Zaman and Shutt, 2022; Alberti et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sharma et al., 2021b; Cartoni and Martinou, 2009; Zaman and Shutt, 2022; Alberti et al., 2024

claim: Mitochondrial fragmentation associated with pathogenic MFN2 variants can be attributed to reduced activity of MFN2-dependent fusion and a subsequent relative increase of DRP1-dependent mitochondrial fission.
source: This can be attributed to reduced activity of MFN2-dependent fusion associated with these variants and a subsequent relative increase of DRP1-dependent mitochondrial fission.
evidence: Stated as an inference based on established knowledge about MFN2 function

claim: MFN2D414V-expressing fibroblasts showed shorter, more fragmented mitochondrial networks compared to control fibroblasts, reflected by reductions in both bounding box and ellipsoid principle axis lengths and increased sphericity.
source: As reported previously, MFN2D414V-expressing fibroblasts showed shorter, more fragmented mitochondrial networks compared to control fibroblasts, reflected by reductions in both bounding box and ellipsoid principle axis lengths and increased sphericity (Figure 4A and E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C; Sharma et al., 2021b).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 4A and E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C, with citation to Sharma et al., 2021b

claim: Treatment with halofuginone, 0357, or 3610 increased mitochondrial length in control fibroblasts.
source: Treatment with halofuginone, 0357, or 3610 increased mitochondrial length in control fibroblasts (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 4A–D

claim: The increase in mitochondrial length in control fibroblasts induced by halofuginone, 0357, or 3610 was inhibited by co-treatment with ISRIB.
source: These changes were inhibited by co-treatment with ISRIB, confirming these effects can be attributed to ISR activation.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data

claim: Treatment with halofuginone, 0357, or 3610 increased mitochondrial length and reduced sphericity in MFN2D414V-expressing patient fibroblasts to levels similar to those observed in control fibroblasts, with halofuginone showing the largest effect.
source: Intriguingly, all three compounds also increased mitochondrial length and reduced sphericity in MFN2D414V-expressing patient fibroblasts to levels similar to those observed in control fibroblasts, with halofuginone showing the largest effect (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data shown in Figure 4E–H

claim: The increase in mitochondrial elongation in MFN2D414V-expressing patient fibroblasts was reversed by co-treatment with ISRIB.
source: Again, this increase in mitochondrial elongation was reversed by co-treatment with ISRIB.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data

claim: Mitochondrial fragmentation is often induced through a mechanism involving stress-dependent increases in the activity of the pro-fission GTPase DRP1.
source: Mitochondrial fragmentation is often induced through a mechanism involving stress-dependent increases in the activity of the pro-fission GTPase DRP1 (Chan, 2020; Giacomello et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan, 2020; Giacomello et al., 2020

claim: Activation of the ISR kinase PERK during ER stress promotes mitochondrial elongation through a mechanism involving inhibition of DRP1.
source: Activation of the ISR kinase PERK during ER stress promotes mitochondrial elongation through a mechanism involving inhibition of DRP1 (Perea et al., 2023b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Perea et al., 2023b

claim: Pharmacologic activation of the ISR using both GCN2 and HRI-activating compounds blocks the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in ionomycin-treated cells.
source: Consistent with this idea, we show that pharmacologic activation of the ISR using both GCN2 and HRI-activating compounds blocks the accumulation of fragmented mitochondria in ionomycin-treated cells – a condition that promotes mitochondrial fragmentation through increased DRP1-dependent fission (Ji et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2017).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript, with citations to Ji et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2017

claim: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial-targeted proteins are causatively associated with the onset and pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative disorders, including CMT, spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA), and spastic paraplegia.
source: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial-targeted proteins are causatively associated with the onset and pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative disorders, including CMT, spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA), and spastic paraplegia (Chan, 2020; Sharma et al., 2021a; Gorman et al., 2016; Lightowlers et al., 2015; Song et al., 2021; Deshwal et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chan, 2020; Sharma et al., 2021a; Gorman et al., 2016; Lightowlers et al., 2015; Song et al., 2021; Deshwal et al., 2020

claim: In many neurodegenerative diseases, mitochondrial fragmentation is linked to pathologic mitochondrial dysfunctions, such as reduced respiratory chain activity, decreased mtDNA, and increased apoptotic signaling.
source: In many of these diseases, mitochondrial fragmentation is linked to pathologic mitochondrial dysfunctions, such as reduced respiratory chain activity, decreased mtDNA, and increased apoptotic signaling.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about mitochondrial dysfunction in disease

claim: Pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial fragmentation mitigates cellular and mitochondrial pathologies associated with many neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Intriguingly, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial fragmentation mitigates cellular and mitochondrial pathologies associated with many of these diseases, highlighting the critical link between mitochondrial fragmentation and disease pathogenesis (Das et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2023b; Mou and Li, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Das et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2023b; Mou and Li, 2019

claim: Over 70% of cases of axonal CMT are associated with pathogenic MFN2 variants.
source: Regardless, our results are of substantial interest because over 70% of cases of axonal CMT are associated with pathogenic MFN2 variants, and to date, no disease-modifying therapies are available for any genetic subtype of CMT (Yoshimura et al., 2019; Pisciotta et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yoshimura et al., 2019; Pisciotta et al., 2021

claim: No disease-modifying therapies are available for any genetic subtype of CMT.
source: over 70% of cases of axonal CMT are associated with pathogenic MFN2 variants, and to date, no disease-modifying therapies are available for any genetic subtype of CMT (Yoshimura et al., 2019; Pisciotta et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yoshimura et al., 2019; Pisciotta et al., 2021

claim: ISR signaling promotes adaptive remodeling of many aspects of mitochondrial biology, including proteostasis, electron transport chain activity, phospholipid synthesis, and apoptotic signaling.
source: Apart from morphology, ISR signaling also promotes adaptive remodeling of many other aspects of mitochondrial biology, including proteostasis, electron transport chain activity, phospholipid synthesis, and apoptotic signaling (Hori et al., 2002; Han et al., 2013; Rainbolt et al., 2013; Balsa et al., 2019; Barad et al., 2023; Latorre-Muro et al., 2021; Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hori et al., 2002; Han et al., 2013; Rainbolt et al., 2013; Balsa et al., 2019; Barad et al., 2023; Latorre-Muro et al., 2021; Lebeau et al., 2018; Perea et al., 2023b

claim: Halofuginone-dependent GCN2 activation restored cellular ER stress sensitivity and mitochondrial electron transport chain activity in cells deficient in the alternative ISR kinase PERK.
source: For example, we previously showed that halofuginone-dependent GCN2 activation restored cellular ER stress sensitivity and mitochondrial electron transport chain activity in cells deficient in the alternative ISR kinase PERK (Perea et al., 2023a) – a model of neurodegenerative diseases associated with reduced PERK activity such as PSP and AD (Park et al., 2023; Yuan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Perea et al., 2023a; Park et al., 2023; Yuan et al., 2018

claim: PERK deficiency is a model of neurodegenerative diseases associated with reduced PERK activity such as PSP and AD.
source: cells deficient in the alternative ISR kinase PERK (Perea et al., 2023a) – a model of neurodegenerative diseases associated with reduced PERK activity such as PSP and AD (Park et al., 2023; Yuan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Park et al., 2023; Yuan et al., 2018

claim: The HRI activator BtdCPU activates the ISR through a mechanism involving mitochondrial uncoupling and subsequent mitochondrial fragmentation.
source: For example, the HRI activator BtdCPU activates the ISR through a mechanism involving mitochondrial uncoupling and subsequent mitochondrial fragmentation (Perea et al., 2023a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Perea et al., 2023a

claim: The nucleoside mimetic compounds 0357 and 3610 activate the ISR downstream of HRI and show selectivity for the ISR relative to other stress-responsive signaling pathways.
source: Here, we identify two nucleoside mimetic compounds that activate the ISR downstream of HRI and show selectivity for the ISR relative to other stress-responsive signaling pathways, providing new tools to probe mitochondrial remodeling induced by ISR kinase activation.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: The low potency of compounds 0357 and 3610 limits their translational potential to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in disease.
source: However, the low potency of these compounds limits their translational potential to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in disease, necessitating the identification of new, highly selective ISR kinase-activating compounds.
evidence: Stated as an inference based on the observed low potency of the compounds

claim: Pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases represents a potential strategy to mitigate pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation associated with human disease.
source: This suggests that pharmacologic activation of the ISR represents a potential strategy to mitigate pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation associated with human disease.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the findings in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases HRI or GCN2 promotes adaptive mitochondrial elongation and prevents mitochondrial fragmentation induced by the calcium ionophore ionomycin.
source: Here, we show that pharmacologic activation of the ISR kinases HRI or GCN2 promotes adaptive mitochondrial elongation and prevents mitochondrial fragmentation induced by the calcium ionophore ionomycin.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of the ISR reduces mitochondrial fragmentation and restores basal mitochondrial morphology in patient fibroblasts expressing the pathogenic D414V variant of MFN2.
source: Further, we show that pharmacologic activation of the ISR reduces mitochondrial fragmentation and restores basal mitochondrial morphology in patient fibroblasts expressing the pathogenic D414V variant of the pro-fusion mitochondrial GTPase MFN2 associated with neurological dysfunctions, including ataxia, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases is a potential strategy to prevent pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation induced by disease-relevant chemical and genetic insults.
source: These results identify pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases as a potential strategy to prevent pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation induced by disease-relevant chemical and genetic insults, further motivating the pursuit of highly selective ISR kinase-activating compounds as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction implicated in diverse human diseases.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the findings in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of different ISR kinases can prevent mitochondrial fragmentation induced by disease-relevant chemical or genetic insults.
source: Here, we show that pharmacologic activation of different ISR kinases can prevent mitochondrial fragmentation induced by disease-relevant chemical or genetic insults.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of different ISR kinases can mitigate pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation induced by diverse disease-associated pathologic insults.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that pharmacologic activation of different ISR kinases can mitigate pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation induced by diverse disease-associated pathologic insults.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the findings in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases can be broadly applied to quell mitochondrial fragmentation in diseases associated with overactive DRP1.
source: These results support a model whereby pharmacologic activation of different ISR kinases promotes organelle elongation by inhibiting DRP1 and suggests that pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases can be broadly applied to quell mitochondrial fragmentation in the myriad diseases associated with overactive DRP1.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the findings in the manuscript

claim: Pharmacologic activation of the ISR mitigates mitochondrial fragmentation in patient fibroblasts homozygous for the disease-associated D414V MFN2 variant.
source: Herein, we show that pharmacologic activation of the ISR mitigates mitochondrial fragmentation in patient fibroblasts homozygous for the disease-associated D414V MFN2 variant.
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript

claim: Further study is necessary to determine the impact of ISR activation in cells from heterozygous patients expressing pathogenic MFN2 variants associated with CMT2A.
source: This finding highlights the potential for pharmacologic ISR activation to restore basal mitochondrial network morphology in cells expressing pathogenic MFN2 variants, although further study is necessary to determine the impact of ISR activation in cells from heterozygous patients expressing pathogenic MFN2 variants associated with CMT2A, the most common clinical phenotype associated with this disease.
evidence: Stated as a limitation and future direction

claim: Pharmacologic ISR kinase activation has potential to broadly mitigate pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation associated with the expression of disease-related, pathogenic variants of other mitochondrial proteins.
source: Apart from MFN2 variants, our results also highlight the potential for pharmacologic ISR kinase activation to broadly mitigate pathologic mitochondrial fragmentation associated with the expression of disease-related, pathogenic variants of other mitochondrial proteins, which we are continuing to explore.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion and future direction based on the findings

claim: Pharmacologic activators of ISR kinases could more broadly influence cellular and mitochondrial biology in disease states through the adaptive remodeling of multiple mitochondrial pathways.
source: While we specifically focus on defining the potential for pharmacologic activation of ISR kinases to rescue mitochondrial morphology in disease models, the potential of ISR activation to promote adaptive remodeling of other mitochondrial functions suggests that pharmacologic activators of ISR kinases could more broadly influence cellular and mitochondrial biology in disease states through the adaptive remodeling of these other pathways.
evidence: Stated as a speculation based on known ISR functions

claim: Compounds that activate ISR kinases are predicted to promote the direct remodeling of mitochondrial pathways to influence multiple mitochondrial functions.
source: Compounds that activate other ISR kinases are similarly predicted to promote the direct remodeling of mitochondrial pathways to influence these and other functions.
evidence: Stated as a prediction based on known ISR functions

claim: The potential for many previously reported ISR kinase-activating compounds to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in human disease is limited by factors including lack of selectivity for the ISR or a specific ISR kinase, off-target activities, or low therapeutic windows.
source: However, the potential for many of these compounds to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in human disease is limited by factors including lack of selectivity for the ISR or a specific ISR kinase, off-target activities, or low therapeutic windows (Perea et al., 2023a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Perea et al., 2023a

claim: It will be important to optimize the pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) profiles of ISR kinase activators to selectively enhance adaptive, protective ISR signaling in disease-relevant tissues, independent of maladaptive ISR signaling often associated with chronic, stress-dependent activation of this pathway.
source: As we and others continue identifying next-generation ISR kinase activators with improved translational potential, it will be important to optimize the pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) profiles of these compounds to selectively enhance adaptive, protective ISR signaling in disease-relevant tissues, independent of maladaptive ISR signaling often associated with chronic, stress-dependent activation of this pathway (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated as a future direction, with citations to Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016

claim: Improvements in ISR kinase activators can be achieved by defining optimized compound properties and dosing regimens to control the timing and extent of pathway activity.
source: As described previously for activators the IRE1 arm of the UPR, such improvements can be achieved by defining optimized compound properties and dosing regimens to control the timing and extent of pathway activity (Madhavan et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Madhavan et al., 2022

claim: Pharmacologic ISR kinase activation is anticipated to be established as a viable approach to treat mitochondrial dysfunction associated with etiologically diverse diseases.
source: Thus, as we and others continue pursuing pharmacologic ISR kinase activation as a strategy to target mitochondrial dysfunction in disease, we anticipate that we will continue to learn more about the central role for this pathway in adapting mitochondria during stress and establish pharmacologic ISR kinase activation as a viable approach to treat mitochondrial dysfunction associated with etiologically diverse diseases.
evidence: Stated as a future expectation and goal

claim: An automated image analysis pipeline using Imaris software was implemented to quantify mitochondrial elongation in MEF cells stably expressing mitochondrial-targeted GFP.
source: To address this, we implemented an automated image analysis pipeline using Imaris software to quantify mitochondrial elongation in MEF cells stably expressing mitochondrial-targeted GFP (mtGFP) treated with our compounds (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A); (Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: Described as a methodological approach, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and citation to Wang et al., 2012

claim: Z-stack confocal images of mtGFP-expressing MEF cells were collected and processed using a deconvolution filter in FIJI to reduce the background and enhance the fluorescent signal.
source: We collected Z-stack confocal images of mtGFP-expressing MEF cells (MEFmtGFP) and processed images using a deconvolution filter in FIJI to reduce the background and enhance the fluorescent signal.
evidence: Described as a methodological approach

claim: The 'Surfaces' module on Imaris was used to generate three-dimensional (3D) segmentation models of mitochondria visible in the deconvolved Z-stacks.
source: We used the 'Surfaces' module on Imaris to generate three-dimensional (3D) segmentation models of mitochondria visible in the deconvolved Z-stacks.
evidence: Described as a methodological approach

claim: Using the surfaces module, parameters defining mitochondrial shape were quantified, including bounding box length, sphericity, and ellipsoid principal axis length.
source: Using the surfaces module, we quantified parameters defining mitochondrial shape, including bounding box length, sphericity, and ellipsoid principal axis length (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Described as a methodological approach, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: The primary screen used the ATF4-FLuc translational reporter of the ISR to screen the ~3k nucleoside mimetic analog compound library at 10 µM and monitored ATF4-FLuc activity 8 hr after treatment.
source: In this screen, we used the ATF4-FLuc translational reporter of the ISR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A; Yang et al., 2023a) We confirmed that ISR-activating stressors including the ER stressor thapsigargin (Tg) and the ATP synthase inhibitor oligomycin A (OA) robustly activated this reporter (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B). We then used this reporter to screen the ~3k nucleoside mimetic analog compound library (10 µM) and monitored ATF4-FLuc activity 8 hr after treatment.
evidence: Described as a methodological approach, with references to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and 1B and citation to Yang et al., 2023a

claim: MEFmtGFP cells were pretreated for 6 hr with halofuginone or HRI-activating compounds (0357 and 3610) and subsequently challenged with ionomycin, and mitochondrial morphology was monitored over a 15 min timecourse.
source: We pretreated MEFmtGFP cells for 6 hr with the GCN2 activator halofuginone or our two HRI-activating compounds (0357 and 3610) and subsequently challenged these cells with ionomycin. We then monitored mitochondrial morphology over a 15 min timecourse.
evidence: Described as a methodological approach

claim: Wild-type human fibroblasts and patient fibroblasts expressing MFN2D414V were treated with halofuginone or HRI-activating compounds 0357 and 3610 and mitochondrial network morphology was monitored by staining with MitoTracker.
source: To test this, we treated wild-type human fibroblasts and patient fibroblasts expressing MFN2D414V with halofuginone or our two HRI-activating compounds 0357 and 3610 and monitored mitochondrial network morphology by staining with MitoTracker.
evidence: Described as a methodological approach

claim: Primary fibroblast cells were isolated from partial thickness skin biopsy from a patient who provided written informed consent for research studies using human tissues.
source: Primary fibroblast cells were isolated from partial thickness skin biopsy, as previously described (Sharma et al., 2021b; Martens et al., 2020), from a patient who provided written informed consent for research studies using human tissues (University of Calgary Conjoint Research Ethics Board REB17-0850).
evidence: Described as a methodological approach, with citations to Sharma et al., 2021b; Martens et al., 2020

claim: Clinical information regarding the patient expressing MFN2D414V included ataxia, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss.
source: Clinical information regarding this participant was previously reported and included ataxia, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss (Sharma et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sharma et al., 2021b
